question: Should OpenClaw treat the first running event for pending non-silent background/native tasks as a requester-visible acknowledgement even when `notifyPolicy` is `done_only`?
rationale: The code path now looks mechanically coherent, but this changes live channel message volume and ordering for existing task workflows, which is a task-delivery UX policy choice rather than a purely local correctness question.

options.title: Accept start acknowledgements
options.body: Merge this direction after normal gates if maintainers want `done_only` to mean quiet progress plus one visible start and one terminal update.

options.title: Keep done_only terminal-only
options.body: Ask the contributor to restrict start notices to explicit `state_changes` or another maintainer-approved opt-in surface.

options.title: Pause for broader notification policy
options.body: Hold this PR if start, progress, parent-review, and terminal task visibility should be redesigned together.

recommendation.title: Accept start acknowledgements
recommendation.body: Merge this direction after normal gates if maintainers want `done_only` to mean quiet progress plus one visible start and one terminal update.
